title: compact runtime overlay + delta-patch apply hook for smaller airgap bundles
author: Arjun Patel
release_notes:
- Add compact runtime overlay to reduce airgap bundle size by ~40-50% across common distro targets.
- Introduce an atomic 'apply-delta' installer hook that applies binary deltas on top of a slim runtime overlay for fast in-place upgrades.
- Add k0s distro support for overlay apply; improvements to helm/chart rendering for constrained environments.
description:
Context and motivation: Air-gapped/private customers have repeatedly asked for smaller offline bundles and safer in-place upgrades. Large full-image bundles (20+ GB) are costly to distribute and slow to apply in constrained environments. This change introduces a compact runtime overlay format plus a delta-patch apply hook so subsequent upgrades can be shipped as small binary deltas and applied atomically.

What this PR does (summary): Compacts the runtime footprint by serializing only the files needed for the runtime overlay (stripped binaries, minimal lib set, curated kernel modules) and adds a deterministic delta generation/consumption flow. The installer gains a new hook 'apply-delta' which verifies, extracts, and applies a delta to the existing overlay using a transactional swap (write-to-temp + atomic rename). If patch apply fails, the hook rolls back cleanly to the previous overlay.

Design notes: - Overlay format: tar.xz with deterministic ordering + manifest checksums to keep reproducible artifacts and stable delta generation. - Delta format: bsdiff-based binary deltas + signed manifest. We opted for bsdiff/bs patching due to its small patch sizes for our binary workloads. - Atomicity: the hook writes to an overlay staging directory, runs a validation (checksum + smoke start), then swaps symlink to new overlay; a cleanup step removes the old overlay on success. - Distro support: k0s and kubeadm flows are updated to accept an overlay path; we added a lightweight shim to map overlay contents to expected kubelet/systemd paths for k0s. Existing k3s/rke2 flows are unchanged but opt-in to delta apply via configuration.

Commits (high level): - Add compact-overlay build pipeline and shrinkwrap script (scripts/overlay/build-compact.sh) - Introduce apply-delta hook with validation/rollback logic (installer/hooks/apply-delta.sh) - Terraform: add airgap_registry module changes for delta manifests and retention (terraform/modules/airgap_registry/main.tf) - Helm: add values-airgap-compact.yaml and chart templates to mount overlays (charts/redwood/templates/overlay-config.yaml) - Tests: unit + integration harness for delta apply (test/airgap/delta-apply-integration.sh) - Docs: docs/airgap/compact-overlay.md and ops notes (docs/airgap/compact-overlay.md)

Files touched (representative): - scripts/overlay/build-compact.sh - installer/hooks/apply-delta.sh - installer/manifests/overlays/compact-overlay.yaml - charts/redwood/values-airgap-compact.yaml - terraform/modules/airgap_registry/main.tf - test/airgap/delta-apply-integration.sh - docs/airgap/compact-overlay.md - packaging/ci/generate-compact-bundle.yml

Testing and CI: Local unit tests for the hook logic, luacheck/shfmt on shell scripts, and a lightweight integration test that runs in a small VM simulating an offline node. CI required adding a new pipeline job 'airgap-bundle:compact' which runs bundle generation and verifies delta application against a reference overlay. The initial CI run flagged a flaky timing assertion in the integration smoke test (flake in smoke-start check). I fixed the test (stabilize startup wait and probe), re-ran CI and all checks passed. CI checks: unit, lint, airgap-bundle:compact, integration (all green).

Upgrade/rollback behaviour: The apply-delta hook will not be enabled by default for existing customers; it is gated behind an opt-in flag in the installer config (installer.flags.use_compact_overlay=true). When enabled, the installer will attempt to apply delta patches in-place. If the apply fails at any step, the hook performs a rollback and surfaces a clear error explaining the failure reason and attempted rollback. We included a migration script (scripts/overlay/migrate-to-compact.sh) to convert full bundles to compact overlays when customers want to move to the new format.

Security and signing: All compact overlay artifacts and delta manifests are signed with our existing bundle signing keys. The hook verifies signatures before application. We also added size and checksum sanity checks to reduce risk of partial/tampered deltas.

Ops/runbook notes: See docs/airgap/compact-overlay.md for step-by-step: 1) How to generate compact bundles and deltas 2) How to upload artifacts to an airgap registry 3) Enabling the apply-delta hook and safe rollback commands. The PR includes a short 'quick rollback' helper that operators can run to force reversion in case of CI/test environments.

Backwards compatibility and migration: The compact overlay is backward compatible at the installer API level. Existing full-image bundles continue to work. The delta apply logic is opt-in and requires manifest/version metadata; we added migration tooling to allow incremental opt-in.

Performance/size impact: On our internal sample clusters (Ubuntu 22.04 k0s + kubeadm), compact overlays reduced bundle size by 42-48% and typical deltas are 6-12% of the full bundle size depending on binary churn. This should materially reduce distribution costs and upgrade window times for customers with limited bandwidth.

Known limitations: - Delta generation currently runs in a CI job and requires access to both previous and next compact artifacts; customers with strict airgap constraints will need to stage deltas in their registry. - Very high-binary-churn releases may result in larger deltas; fallback to full bundle is supported.

Rollout plan: 1) Internal dogfood on staging clusters for two weeks (completed) 2) Invite-only pilot with three customers on opt-in mode (planned, Jan 2026) 3) General availability after pilot feedback and final docs.

Related work: ENG-2451 (compact overlays), ENG-2478 (delta apply hooks).

If you're reviewing: focus on the installer hook for atomicity/rollback semantics, the overlay manifest format, and the Terraform changes for delta retention. Small followups expected: add progress reporting metrics to installer console and add a chart value to control delta retention policy.

review_thread: Maya Chen (2025-11-13): Can the staging swap be done with a symlink update only? We want minimal inode churn on slow filesystems.

Author Arjun Patel (2025-11-13): We use a symlink swap as the final step; staging writes to a parallel directory to avoid partial states. Added comment and code to ensure atomic rename on supported filesystems; fallback is a copy+rename with checksum validation.
Luis Romero (2025-11-18): Verify the signature verification path refuses unsigned deltas. Also add clearer error logs for signature mismatches.
Author Arjun Patel (2025-11-18): Added explicit signature check with logging and a failing exit code; added unit test for unsigned delta rejection.
Priya Nair (2025-11-25): Integration test flaked on startup probe — suggest increasing timeout and probing kubelet health instead of generic process check.
Author Arjun Patel (2025-11-26): Updated integration probe to check kubelet health endpoint and added exponential backoff; re-ran CI.
Maya Chen (2025-11-30): Approving, left one minor nit on script logging verbosity.
Luis Romero (2025-12-01): LGTM — small terraform nit suggested in PR comments (retention default lowered to 90 days).
notes_to_ops: Operators: to pilot, generate a compact bundle with 'scripts/overlay/build-compact.sh --source <full-bundle> --out <compact.tar.xz>' and generate deltas via the CI job or use 'scripts/overlay/generate-delta.sh'. Upload artifacts to your airgap registry and enable installer flag 'use_compact_overlay=true'. To force rollback: run installer/hooks/force-rollback.sh with the previous overlay name. See docs/airgap/compact-overlay.md for full commands.
